scenario: Bought 1 Jan 2025 for 10,000, still owned on 1 Sep 2026; valued 8,000 on 1 Jun 2026; a collision repaired for 1,400 and settled by the insurer for 1,000
derivation: Spec 7.7: period 1 Jan 2025 to today, 1 Sep 2026. Running costs = fuel 600 + repair 1,400 = 2,000 over 2 entries, net of the insurance payout of the incident dated in the period (1,000): 2,000 - 1,000 = 1,000 (the payout is its own line, not an entry).

Depreciation: price 10,000 - latest value 8,000 (1 Jun 2026) = 2,000 lost; it is measured to the value's date, so the total is 1,000 + 2,000 = 3,000 labelled 'depreciation to 1 Jun 2026'. The valuation is 3 months old, so not stale.
Distance: 10,000 mi on 1 Jan 2025 to 20,000 mi on 1 Sep 2026 = 10,000 mi = 16,093.44 km; to the valuation date, 1 Jan 2025 to 1 Jun 2026 (18,000 mi) = 8,000 mi = 12,874.752 km.
Per km, 6 places: running 1,000 / 16,093.44 = 0.062137; depreciation 2,000 / 12,874.752 = 0.155343; together 0.217480 a km = 0.35 a mile (running 0.1, depreciation 0.25).

Per month: 21 calendar months touched (Jan 2025 to Sep 2026): running 1,000 / 21 = 47.619048. Depreciation per year = 2,000 x 12 / 17 months (1 Jan 2025 to 1 Jun 2026) = 1,411.765, per month 117.647083. Together 165.266 (shown 165.27).

page: from 2 entries logged between 1 Jan 2025 and 1 Sept 2026, less £1,000.00 of insurance payouts
Total: £1,000.00 of running costs + £2,000.00 of depreciation = £3,000.00.
